rv.q: “Refuge” offers up a wall of rich sound, driven by a guitarist and lead musician named Laura Murillo Hart, who powerfully conducts the piece as she goes, even as pulsing puppet critters (Adolfo Romero is the designer) move on by and a wave of humanity fights the inhumane conditions.
Theo Ubique's new play, Refuge , should be required viewing for everyone on either side of this issue.
Refuge is a moving performance unlikely to be forgotten and surely not to be missed.
This important tale is unlike any other musical experienced on the Theo Ubique stage.

However heavy-handed some of the plot points, the production never fails to engage the audience with incredibly vivid images of an endless and deadly land with a border no thicker than a piece of rope.
The music and the acting is truly enough to make this an enjoyable experience that will give you pause to speak about what you saw and what you felt.

cn.t: Critics praise "Refuge" as a powerful and beautiful exploration of immigration at the Texas-Mexico border, with reviewers highlighting its emotional resonance, multidisciplinary storytelling, and ability to foster deep compassion for migrants' experiences.
